stop_rule: Do not further tune King Rail latent-state models on the same response. Move the generated prediction to response-frozen replication.
primary_general_hypothesis: Habitat/salinity niche breadth predicts temporal site-use memory: habitat specialists should repeatedly use a narrower set of sites and therefore show stronger prior-site persistence than habitat-flexible species.

per_species_endpoints.prior_site_fraction: fraction of post-initialization positives at previously detected sites
per_species_endpoints.gap_return_fraction: fraction of post-initialization positives that return at a previously detected site after at least one observed gap

primary_cross_species_prediction.statement: Among the ten non-King-Rail species, habitat specialists (low- or high-salinity associated) have higher post-initialization prior-site fractions than habitat-flexible species.
primary_cross_species_prediction.response: prior_site_fraction = post-initialization positives at sites detected previously / all post-initialization positives
primary_cross_species_prediction.contrast: mean specialist prior_site_fraction - mean flexible prior_site_fraction
primary_cross_species_prediction.test: Exact label-permutation test over the fixed 6 specialist and 4 flexible non-King-Rail species; one-sided alternative > 0.

secondary_prediction.statement: After first-positive initialization is removed, broad cumulative history should reduce unsupported positives more consistently than merely interpreting every unsupported detection as long-distance movement.
secondary_prediction.output: species-wise paired table of immediate versus cumulative unsupported positive counts at each fixed scale

claim_boundary: This panel tests temporal site-use/detection geometry, not true movement routes.
Published habitat classes are fixed before temporal sequence access.
No alpha-code may be dropped because its result is inconvenient; sparse species are reported as non-estimable.
King Rail is the hypothesis-generating seed and is excluded from the primary prospective specialist-versus-flexible test.
Memory-rescue versus gap-return correlation is descriptive because the two metrics share underlying events.

published_habitat_classification.rule: Classification is frozen from the published occupancy interpretation, not derived from the temporal sequences opened by this programme.

secondary_cross_species_predictions.statement: Specialists have higher same-site gap-return fractions than flexible species.
Extending source memory from immediate-previous to cumulative history reduces unsupported positives, especially in species with strong site persistence.
secondary_cross_species_predictions.role: mechanistic diagnostic only; not used as an independent test of persistence because the quantities share events
